findings.title: T5 writes long numbers in full in the tape, the sorted tapes and the end positions of 'Two games compared'
findings.location: site/src/components/tools/T05NumbersGameLab.svelte:214-215 (listText, tuple), :552-553 (snippet cells), used at :601 (data-out="tape"), :787-788 (sortedA, sortedB), :795 and :798 (endA, endB)
findings.claim: T5 shortens a long value only on the nodes, the tally bars, the products D and M and the dimension; its listText, tuple and cells helpers never call shortValue, so a fired number or an end position of more than 12 digits is written out in full.
findings.expected: SPEC 4.0 'Long numbers': a value of more than 12 digits is shown shortened ('1.2345... x 10^19 (20 digits)'), with the exact digits in the table view, the tooltip and every export. The same rule was applied to T5's dimension (RT-FIX P3-RT-03-03) and to T12's string viewer (RT-FIX P5-RT-03-01).
findings.observed: Load /tools/numbers/?g=A2&c=n&s=12345678901234567890,-1, a valid link (SPEC 6.6 allows 40 digits). Node 1 shows shortened, with data-value 12345678901234567890. Fire node 1. data-out="tape" reads '12345678901234567890'. In the compared tab, data-out="sortedA" reads '12345678901234567890' and data-out="endA" holds '12345678901234567890' and '12345678901234567889' in full. None of them has a tooltip.

findings.title: Satake data routed to the worker can come back changed, or never settle: restrictedBoard of E7 and E8 does not survive the worker wire
findings.location: site/src/lib/worker.ts:138-145 (onmessage: p.resolve(deserialize(reply.result)) with no catch); site/src/lib/workerWire.ts serialize (a Board becomes { $board: specOf(board) }) and deserialize ($board rebuilt with resolveBoard)
findings.claim: A Board inside a worker result is sent as its name or its matrix and rebuilt with resolveBoard on the main side. The 0-node board of a compact form cannot be rebuilt: the NotABoard thrown inside onmessage leaves the engineCall promise pending. A named restricted board whose matrix is in orbit order comes back as the standard board of that name.
findings.expected: CONTRACTS 4: the worker message re-throws errors 'on the main side as the same class'. worker.ts header: 'a worker failure rejects the promise'. E-9: a call routed to the worker answers 'behind the same promise' with the same result it gives on the main thread.
findings.observed: engineCall('restrictedBoard', [compact E8, black 1..8], { board: E8, kind: 'satake' }) goes to the worker, where whereToRun says 'worker'. The promise is still pending after 2 s, and the stub worker records an uncaught 'NotABoard: an adjacency matrix needs at least one node'. The same happens on the wire for e7(-133) and e8(-248). For e8(-24), main thread: rb.board has labels [4,3,2,1] and Cartan [[2,-1,0,0],[-1,2,-2,0],[0,-1,2,-1],[0,0,-1,2]]. Through the wire: labels [1,2,3,4] and Cartan [[2,-1,0,0],[-1,2,-1,0],[0,-2,2,-1],[0,0,-1,2]], so rb.board no longer agrees with rb.cartan. No reader reaches either effect today: T13 makes no call for a pair without a white node (MERGE ruling (4) on P6-A1) and never reads rb.board.
findings.reproduction: From a clean checkout of f07eec6 plus this branch's files: npm ci; TMPDIR=<fresh dir> npx vitest run --project site-unit redteam-RT-03-p6-worker-wire (4 tests fail: E7 e7(-133), E8 e8(-24), E8 e8(-248), and the compact form through engineCall).
findings.specRef: CONTRACTS.md 4 (worker message, serialization, 'errors re-thrown on the main side as the same class'); SPEC.md 5.1 E-9 item 3 (Satake data for E7 and E8 in the worker); RT-03 lens attack 22
findings.proposedFix: Catch a deserialize failure in onmessage and reject the pending promise with it. Serialize a Board in a result with its matrix and labels, and its name, whenever it is not the standard board of its name. Either let a 0-node board round-trip or refuse it in the worker, so the error crosses as an error.

findings.title: exportLaTeX writes TeX with 'undefined' and missing node names for lists that have a hole, instead of refusing
findings.location: site/src/lib/export.ts:686-692 (edgeList: Array.prototype.every skips holes), :697-709 (tikzGraph: nodes.map skips holes), :711-729 (tikzPoints: points.map and forEach skip holes)
findings.claim: The tikz-graph and tikz-points writers check their lists with map, every and forEach, which skip the holes of a sparse array. A hole in the vertices, the points or an edge passes every check and reaches the TeX text.
findings.expected: exportLaTeX 'Throws RangeError, naming the fault, on data it cannot write' (export.ts:737, the CONTRACTS 4 function, plan). An explicit undefined in the same place is already a RangeError. The P6-A1 review found the same class of defect in satake.ts checkPopulation, and it was fixed with a test.
findings.observed: tikz-points with points [[0,0], <hole>, [1,1]] and edges [[0,1]] writes '\draw (0,0) -- undefined;'. tikz-graph with edges [[<hole>, 1]] writes '\draw (nundefined) -- (n1);'. tikz-points with edge [<hole>, 1] writes '\draw undefined -- (1,1);'. tikz-graph with nodes [{x:0,y:0}, <hole>, {x:1,y:1}] writes '\draw (n0) -- (n1);' although no node n1 is defined. None of them throws. T2's and T10's adapters build dense arrays, so no reader reaches this today.
findings.reproduction: From a clean checkout of f07eec6 plus this branch's files: npm ci; TMPDIR=<fresh dir> npx vitest run --project site-unit redteam-RT-03-p6-latex (4 of 7 tests fail).
findings.proposedFix: Read nodes, points and each edge with index loops over 0..length-1 (or Array.from first), so a hole reaches the existing type checks.

findings.title: The Atlas writes the cap of counting games as the literal 60000 in its page sentence and its CSV
findings.claim: The Atlas decides with CAPS.countGamesGroup (atlasData.ts), but the sentence that states the limit on the page and in the CSV types the number, so a change of the cap would leave the stated limit wrong.
findings.expected: CONTRACTS 2.3: caps come from CAPS and are used once. RT-03 lens attack 36 counts a duplicated literal with the right value as minor.
findings.observed: AtlasSheet.astro:266 reads 'The number of complete games from all ones is not offered for a group of more than 60000 elements; ...'. downloads.ts:124 writes 'not offered for a group of more than 60000 elements'. Both are literal text, not CAPS.countGamesGroup.
findings.reproduction: From a clean checkout of f07eec6 plus this branch's files: npm ci; TMPDIR=<fresh dir> npx vitest run --project site-unit redteam-RT-03-p6-caps (2 tests fail).
findings.specRef: CONTRACTS.md 2.3 (countGamesGroup: 60000); SPEC.md 5.6 row 'Group order for counting games'; RT-03 lens attack 36

notes: satake.ts (theta, shadow2, admissibility, satake, restrictedBoard, restrictedCoordinates) throws TypeError for a diagram whose board is null or {n: 3}. satakeCatalogue.ts (canonicalPair, matchCatalogue) checks the board and throws RangeError. The P6-A1 plan covers only tau and black, and the P6-A2 review already noted this and left it, so it is not reported.

satakeRecord(name, entry) with restricted_type_display 'C2' on an entry whose restricted board is not B2 (for example the split form of A3) throws a plain EngineError ('restricted board of a C2 record is not B2', the oracle's assert), not a RangeError for a malformed entry. Only reachable from code.
satake on the 0-node board that restrictedBoard returns for a compact form throws RangeError 'a search needs at least one seed', while admissibility on it says admissible. This is outside any tool.

t13/load.ts fetchData returns null when a NotAdmissible comes back from the worker for a pair the main thread judged admissible. refresh then sets neither data nor failure, so 'computing the data in the background' would stay forever. This cannot be reached with a deterministic engine, but it contradicts the plan's 'never a frozen page'.

canonicalPair refusing a board with more than 10000 symmetries by a RangeError follows MERGE's ruling on P6-A2's review. E-10's 'reaching a cap is never thrown' is read there as applying to enumerations only. Not reported.

SPEC 386 and 169 state that the one-way board's root set is infinite [V]. verify.py checks it with the 2000-position cap plus entry growth, and confusions.mdx repeats it as 'verified by computation'. This is SPEC-backed, so it is not a cap inference by the site.

Incidental, outside this lens: confusions.mdx line 75 types '60000' and 'eight' in prose ('verified by computation on the boards of finite type of rank at most eight whose Weyl group has at most 60000 elements').
